critical_bugs: Unhandled exceptions in update_knowledge_from_session() and inspect_project() when deserializing .pkl files; corrupted or malformed session/calibration data will crash the agent without graceful degradation.

Potential KeyError/AttributeError during knowledge merging due to schema drift: loaded objects may lack keys like position_variance_m2, sources_seen, or have incompatible types (e.g., list instead of set), causing crashes on .add() or arithmetic operations.
warnings: Insecure deserialization via pickle.load(); if session directories are exposed to external inputs or untrusted data, malicious payloads could execute arbitrary code.
No input validation for root_path and session_path parameters; relative paths or symlinks could lead to unexpected file system traversal or permission errors.
recommendations: Wrap all pickle.load() calls in try-except blocks catching specific exceptions (pickle.UnpicklingError, EOFError, KeyError) and implement safe fallbacks or logging.
Normalize data structures after loading: e.g., obj['sources_seen'] = set(obj.get('sources_seen', [])) to prevent type mismatches.
Replace pickle with a safer serialization format like JSON or MessagePack for persistent knowledge, as the schema contains only primitive types and nested dicts/lists.
Add lightweight schema validation (e.g., using pydantic or explicit key checks) when loading external .pkl files to ensure compatibility before processing.
